Category:Appraisal.body:
## Overview

The Imperial civil service support [the Throne](../../mixed/titles/The_Throne.md) and all arms of the Imperial government, providing detailed reports for consideration by the Empire's leader every summit. For the most part these reports entail detailed assessments of the latest developments in the Empire, outlining what is known about the situation, what options might exist, and what the implications of those options are. The bulk of these reports are reactionary - the civil servants responding to current events as they are develop between summits.

However, during periods where civil service capacity to produce effective summaries is demonstrably greater than is needed to keep pace with current events, they place this additional capacity at the disposal of the Senate. Doing so allows the Senate to pass a motion of [appraisal](../../in-character/appraisals/Appraisal.md), instructing the civil service to investigate a specific area to see what opportunities if any exist for the Empire to take action.

Category:Archetype.title: Category:Archetype
Category:Archetype.body:
### [The Brass Coast](../../in-character/nations/the-brass-coast/The_Brass_Coast.md)

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| [Dhomiro](../../in-character/nations/the-brass-coast/The_Brass_Coast_leadership.md#dhomiro) | A dhomiro is a member of a Freeborn family who is chosen by the family to be their representative to the wider world; sometimes as a leader, sometimes as an emissary. |
| [Kohan](../../in-character/nations/the-brass-coast/Kohan.md) | Kohan are groups of volunteer and outcast warriors-without-family, who traditionally pledge loyalty to a group of hakima. |
| [Sutannir](../../in-character/nations/the-brass-coast/Sutannir.md) | Sutannir perform inspiring religious ceremonies for the Freeborn, and encourage people to exemplify and celebrate Virtue. |
| [Hakima](../../in-character/nations/the-brass-coast/Hakima.md) | Hakima are highly-organised groups of magic-users whose loyalty is to the nation, not their family. They are taken to be wise. |
| [Corsair](../../in-character/nations/the-brass-coast/Corsair.md) | Freeborn corsairs are traders and privateers who deal with - and raid - barbarian shipping in the Bay of Catazar. |
| [Scrivener](../../in-character/nations/the-brass-coast/The_Brass_Coast_economic_interests.md#scriveners) | Scriveners are Freeborn contract-writers who help traders frame the terms of their deals, and then decorate them with artwork and calligraphy. |

### [Dawn](../../in-character/nations/dawn/Dawn.md)

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| [Earl](../../in-character/nations/dawn/Earl.md) | The Earl of a Dawnish Noble House is the House's leader, who leads the House in all its great achievements and who sets its conditions of membership. |
| [Knight-errant](../../in-character/nations/dawn/Knight-errant.md) | Knights-Errant are engaged in their Test of Mettle. Still technically yeofolk they are expected - and are questing - to prove themselves glorious. |
| [Questing knight](../../in-character/nations/dawn/Questing_knight.md) | Questing Knights are those Knights who have proved themselves worthy in their Test of Mettle and have chosen to keep on questing for ever-greater glory. |
| [Troubadour](../../in-character/religion/Troubadour.md) | A Troubadour is a priest who learns all the stories of their Noble House, past and present, and tells them in poetry and song to inspire their people to greatness. |
| [Witch](../../mixed/magic/lore/Dawn_magical_traditions.md#war-witches) | Witches are Dawnish magic-users. In noble houses, they fight alongside the House's warriors. Most others belong to Weaver Cabals, independent groups of ritual witches which accept both yeofolk and noble members. |
| [Guiser](../../mixed/magic/lore/Dawn_magical_traditions.md#guisers) | Itinerant entertainers who often combine magic with their performances and practice [dramaturgy](../../mixed/magic/lore/Dramaturgy.md). They are often (sometimes justly) accused of being spies, tricksters and mountebanks as well as performers. |
| [Enchanter](../../in-character/nations/dawn/Earl.md#enchanters) | Some Earls who have studied magic choose the title "Earl-Enchanter" or simply "Enchanter". Most learn ritual magic to benefit their people; some build relationships with powerful Summer Eternals. |
| [Seneschal](../../in-character/nations/dawn/Seneschal.md) | A Noble House's Seneschal is a trusted yeofolk who oversees its financial affairs, arranging deals and trades and keeping the House solvent. |
| [Advocate](../../in-character/nations/dawn/Advocate.md) | Dawnish Advocates are yeofolk politicians who navigate the murky waters of Senate politics for their noble masters. |
| [Retainer](../../in-character/nations/dawn/Retainer.md) | A yeofolk Retainer is a Dawnish Noble's most trusted attendant, who works closely with a particular Noble, or sometimes for the whole House. |

### [Highguard](../../in-character/nations/highguard/Highguard.md)

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| [Exarch](../../in-character/nations/highguard/Highguard_leadership.md) | The Exarch, or Exarchs, are those who are appointed by a Highguard Chapter as their leader(s) as determined by the Chapter's creed, or by embodying its principles. |
| [Guardian](../../in-character/nations/highguard/Highguard_military_concerns.md#guardians) | Guardians form the core of Highborn military, taking on a range of roles in defence of their Chapters, and in prosecuting vigilant warfare. |
| [Unconquered](../../in-character/nations/highguard/Unconquered.md) | The Unconquered are Highguard's elite guerrilla troops. They are prone to using ruthless tactics, even operating behind enemy lines, to destroy the enemy's capacity to make war. |
| [Cataphract](../../in-character/nations/highguard/Highguard_military_concerns.md#cataphracts) | Cataphracts are Highguard's elite heavy warriors, who once rode horses into battle but who, in modern times, represent a resolute and unbreakable wall of steel. |
| [Wayfarer](../../in-character/nations/highguard/Highguard_religious_beliefs.md#wayfarers) | Wayfarers are Highborn priests with a long-standing tradition of teaching the truth of [The Way](../../in-character/world/The_Way.md) to the ignorant, and seeking out Exemplars and Paragons born in other lands. |
| [Inquisitor](../../in-character/nations/highguard/Highguard_religious_beliefs.md#the-inquisition) | Highborn Inquisitors are zealous defenders of The Way from those that would threaten it, whether mortal or supernatural. |
| [Steward of the Dead](../../in-character/nations/highguard/Highguard_religious_beliefs.md#stewards-of-the-dead) | Stewards of the Dead dedicate their lives to preserving the legacies of the worthy. This includes the interring of remains as well as the preservation of legacies and tales. |
| [Magister](../../in-character/nations/highguard/Magister.md) | Magisters are the master magicians of Highguard, often with an affinity for Winter Magic. They shape magic using movement, sound and the chime of bells. |
| [Benefactor](../../in-character/nations/highguard/Benefactor.md) | Benefactors are affluent Highborn merchants and tradesfolk who do not pursue wealth for its own sake, but who sponsor individuals, great works and endeavours. |
| [Archivist](../../in-character/nations/highguard/Highguard_history.md#archivists) | Archivists are a unique class of Highborn scholar dedicated to preserving the essence, or truth, of history, over and above accounts and evidence that may seek to undermine that truth. |
| [Grey pilgrim](../../in-character/nations/highguard/Grey_pilgrim.md) | Grey pilgrims are a recent phenomenon. They walk the [trods](../../in-character/nations/navarr/Trod.md) in a crusade to free the souls believed to be trapped between life and death by the [vallorn](../../in-character/nations/navarr/Vallorn.md), but they also oppose heresy and idolatry, convert foreigners to the Way, and seek to guide the other human nations of the Empire toward enlightenment. |

### [Imperial Orcs](../../in-character/nations/imperial-orcs/Imperial_Orcs.md)

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| [Warlord](../../in-character/nations/imperial-orcs/Imperial_Orcs_leadership.md) | Legions chose their own commanders, called warlords, with individuals chosen for their ability to provide clear effective leadership in battle, according to the traditions of the individual legion |
| [Pitfighter](../../in-character/nations/imperial-orcs/Pit-fights.md#pitfighter) | Professional fighters of the Pits in which the Orcs hone their combat skills; trading on the reputation for skill and strength that they have built up in previous fights, pitfighters build their careers until their notoriety means that other orcs begin to seek them out and actively challenge them. |
| [Shaman](../../in-character/nations/imperial-orcs/Shamans.md) | Most orcs only experience communion with the ancestors when battle is upon them but a few individuals - called shamans - are able to hear the voices more frequently; they are almost incessantly surrounded by the constant input of ancestral advice much of it bearing a contradictory or even hostile message. |
| [Preacher](../../in-character/nations/imperial-orcs/Preachers.md) | Those Imperial Orcs who embrace the Way and become priests. |
| [Warcaster](../../mixed/magic/lore/Imperial_Orcs_magical_traditions.md#warcasters) | The highly physical traditions of the Wintermark runesmiths has appealed to some orcs who adopt a similar approach and become Warcasters. |
| [Oathwright](../../mixed/magic/lore/Imperial_Orcs_magical_traditions.md#oathwrights) | Oathwrights believe that the bond between an item and a person affects them both, items may gain worth by being owned and bonded to the right person and the right item affects an individual’s hopes of becoming an ancestor. |
| [Bonesetter](../../in-character/nations/imperial-orcs/Imperial_Orcs_economic_interests.md#bonesetters) | Usually trained apothecaries, physicks or both, Bonesetters are expected to attend to the physical needs of the legion, but their remit runs well beyond this. |
| [Thief-taker](../../in-character/nations/imperial-orcs/Thief-taker.md) | Working closely with Imperial Magistrates, Thief-takers earn their income by collecting bounties on criminals who have fled the law and more rarely by taking payments from private individuals looking to identify perpetrators of crimes. |
| [Reaver](../../in-character/nations/imperial-orcs/Imperial_Orcs_economic_interests.md#reavers) | Soldiers of the Legions who become dedicated to raiding and mercenary work. |

### [The League](../../in-character/nations/the-league/The_League.md)

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| [Merchant Prince](../../in-character/nations/the-league/The_League_leadership.md) | A Merchant Prince is the head of a Guild, the tight-knit mercantile organisations which define the shape of League society. |
| [Bravo](../../in-character/nations/the-league/Bravo.md) | Bravos are the members of the mercenary Free Companies, as rough and rowdy off the battlefield as they are disciplined and professional on it, and immensely proud of their Companies. |
| [Bishop](../../in-character/religion/Bishop.md) | The Bishops of the League are its high priests, who provide Virtuous guidance to any who can afford it, and who compete using the size and influence of their congregations. |
| [Troupe Magician](../../in-character/nations/the-league/Troupe.md) | Troupes are bands of actors who often go masked while performing, and when performing ritual magic. To them, magic is a commodity like any other. |
| [Mountebank](../../in-character/nations/the-league/Mountebank.md) | Mountebanks are street magicians whose tricks may be sleight of hand or genuine magic, many of whom skirt the edges of the law playing short-cons and rigging street games. |
| [Cicisbeo](../../in-character/nations/the-league/The_League_culture_and_customs.md#relationships) | A Cicisbeo is an expensive professional paramour, the only exception to League culture's absolute prohibition on extramarital relations. |

### [The Marches](../../in-character/nations/the-marches/The_Marches.md)

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| [Steward](../../in-character/nations/the-marches/Steward.md) | A steward is the chosen head of a [Marcher household](../../in-character/nations/the-marches/Marcher_household.md). However a steward leads their household only with the consent of the other [yeoman](../../in-character/nations/the-marches/Yeoman_of_the_Marches.md). |
| [Beater](../../in-character/nations/the-marches/The_Marches_military_concerns.md#beaters) | Beaters are a roaming informal police force, learning every part of the land, watching for thieves, vagrants and other ne’er-do-wells. Beaters are often instrumental in settling land disputes between neighbours and they have a vital role in the tradition of [beating the bounds](../../in-character/nations/the-marches/The_Marches_culture_and_customs.md#the-beating-of-the-bounds). Most are skilled foresters or hunters. |
| [Yeoman](../../in-character/nations/the-marches/Yeoman_of_the_Marches.md) | The yeoman is to many the archetypal inhabitant of the Marches. They are a hard people, who own their own land and are well accustomed to a long day working it. Military service is a proud tradition in the Marches, and the majority of yeomen are also soldiers. |
| [Monk](../../in-character/religion/Monastery.md#monks) | Monks minister to the spiritual welfare of the folk around their monastery, largely ignoring [household](../../in-character/nations/the-marches/Marcher_household.md) boundaries. They divide their time between study of the [Imperial Faith](../../in-character/world/The_Way.md) and working the farmlands claimed by the monastery. |
| [Friar](../../in-character/nations/the-marches/The_Marches_religious_beliefs.md#monks-and-friars) | Friars work their own land and provide spiritual advice and counsel to their fellow yeomen in their [household](../../in-character/nations/the-marches/Marcher_household.md). Many also serve as scholars for their community, acting as a chirurgeon, and teaching letters and history to young children. |
| [Landskeeper](../../in-character/nations/the-marches/Landskeeper.md) | A landskeeper is a figure from the Marches magical tradition, who supports the territories or the nation as a whole. Landskeepers can use a variety of methods, from hearth magics and good practical advice to rituals. |
| [Mummer](../../mixed/magic/lore/The_Marches_magical_traditions.md#mummers) | Itinerant entertainers who combine theatrical performance with magic using the techniques of [dramaturgy](../../mixed/magic/lore/Dramaturgy.md). They attend fairs, markets and other regular gatherings performing plays and feats of skill but are often greeted with suspicion and (sometimes unfairly) accused of being tricksters and mountebanks. |
| [Alder](../../in-character/nations/the-marches/The_Marches_economic_interests.md) | Alders are the appointed leaders of [market towns](../../in-character/nations/the-marches/Market_town.md), and are the rough equivalent of the yeomen. In most cases these are wealthy merchants of the town, but often they include prominent town folk such as a friar or blacksmith who lives in the village. |
| [Smith](../../in-character/nations/the-marches/Smith.md) | A skilled crafter who has used a lifetime's experience selling their wares to become a canny trader and experienced negotiator. |
| [Thresher](../../in-character/nations/the-marches/Thresher.md) | A thresher dedicates their life to tracking down those who use magic for nefarious purposes and finding ways to punish them. |

### [Navarr](../../in-character/nations/navarr/Navarr.md)

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| [Brand](../../in-character/nations/navarr/Brand.md) | Navarri who have dedicated themselves to the service of the community, who work tirelessly to aid others without fee. They might be from any profession - Thorn, Vate, blacksmith, tanner, it doesn't matter. They are named for the brand burned into the skin on their left cheekbone. |
| [Dreamspeaker](../../in-character/nations/navarr/Dreamspeaker.md) | Philosophers, visionaries, and activists who aspire to make dreams into reality. |
| [Thorn](../../in-character/nations/navarr/Thorn.md) | A Navarri sworn to service in battle - usually, but not necessarily, a warrior. Always tattooed, they often wear warpaint into battle. |
| [Guide](../../in-character/nations/navarr/Navarr_religious_beliefs.md) | A Navarri who follows the path of the Virtues, and takes it upon themselves to ensure that members of the Empire have found the place in society that they are best suited to. |
| [Broker](../../in-character/nations/navarr/Navarr_economic_interests.md#brokers) | A Navarri who serves as an intermediary between a buyer and a seller, usually claiming some sort of payment from the deal. |
| [Vate](../../mixed/magic/lore/Navarr_magical_traditions.md#vates) | The magical practitioners of Navarr. Often called upon to perform rituals in service of the nation and the Empire, they are the Navarri most trusted to meet with eternals or their heralds. |
| [Vine](../../in-character/nations/navarr/Vine.md) | A Navarr who has dedicated themselves to healing the wounds caused by the vallorn. |

### [Urizen](../../in-character/nations/urizen/Urizen.md)

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| [Arbiter](../../in-character/nations/urizen/Arbiter.md) | An arbiter is the elected leader of the spires, citadels, and temples of Urizen. They are often called on to resolve disputes within a community or to represent it to outsiders. |
| [Architect](../../in-character/nations/urizen/Architect.md) | Architects are interested in economics and how money moves around and the influence it exerts on the world. |
| [Illuminate](../../in-character/nations/urizen/Illuminate.md) | Illuminates use their understanding of the Net of the Heavens to perfect the world; focusing on building up the virtuous... and removing the unvirtuous from prominence. |
| [Mage](../../in-character/nations/urizen/Mage.md) | Mages are magicians motivated by politics. Ambitious and potentially ruthless, a mage understands that all magic is inherently political. |
| [Seer](../../in-character/nations/urizen/Seer.md) | Seers believe that perfect understanding is they key to unlocking the Net of the Heavens. They seek out opportunities to get the right information to the right people so they can make the right decisions. |
| [Sentinel](../../in-character/nations/urizen/Sentinel.md) | Sentinels study the art of war with dedication and commitment that matches that of any magician. |
| [Stargazer](../../in-character/nations/urizen/Stargazer.md) | Stargazers are scholars of magical lore who love magic in all its forms; they are the theoreticians and debaters who push knowledge to its limit. |

| --- | --- |

Category:Asavea.title: Category:Asavea
Category:Asavea.body:
*[Image: Despite its age and internal squabbling, Asavea still maintains a powerful navy.](https://www.profounddecisions.co.uk/empire-wiki/File:From_out_of_the_West.jpg)*

## Overview

A predominantly island culture, Asavea possesses a small empire scattered across a sprawling archipelago, far across the ocean to the west. A timeless and cultured nation, it sees itself as having moved beyond the questioning and struggle of more primitive lands. The Asavean people consider their society to approach perfection; change is considered unnecessary and disruptive and should be avoided as much as possible.

Until around a hundred years ago, the Asavean empire had holdings all over the world. Over the last century they have slowly withdrawn, turning their attention inwards. They appear to be a nation in decline, although they are still powerful enough to maintain a presence on the 'world stage'.

Of particular interest to Imperial citizens are the [Asavean ports](../../mixed/economy/Foreign_ports.md#asavean-archipelago) which are open to trade with the Empire.

## Gifts of Estavus

In Summer 384YE, the eternal Estavus made certain rituals drawing on her power [available to the Empire](../../in-character/winds-of-fortune/Begin_to_speak.md#estavus). The [mystic scrolls of Estavus](../../mixed/magic/rituals/Mystic_scrolls_of_Estavus.md) detail three rituals - [Ramparts of Ashlar](../../mixed/magic/rituals/Mystic_scrolls_of_Estavus.md#ramparts-of-ashlar), [Hammers of Fury](../../mixed/magic/rituals/Mystic_scrolls_of_Estavus.md#hammers-of-fury), and [Accoutrements of War](../../mixed/magic/rituals/Mystic_scrolls_of_Estavus.md#accoutrements-of-war). They are not part of Imperial lore, and cannot be mastered by Imperial citizens, but their capabilities are reasonably common knowledge.

Category:Axos.title: Category:Axos
Category:Axos.body:
*[Image: The Axou helios is an ancient symbol of the Axou people, adopted by the recent Nikitis Axou populist movement.](https://www.profounddecisions.co.uk/empire-wiki/File:Alikos_Helio.jpg)*

## Introduction

The Axos Citadels are located to the south east of the Empire on the far side of [Urizen](../../in-character/nations/urizen/Urizen.md), and sharing a border with [Skoura](../../in-character/foreign-nations/Skoura.md). Their name refers to the chain of citadels that protrude from the crags that line the coast. A people with an ancient history, the Aneleito Axou, or Merciless Axos, are an allegiance of sorcerous city states each answering to a sorcerer king. The Citadels have fierce rivalries with each other, but stand together against the barbarians and the Empire. Due to the catastrophic losses they have suffered, they are more given to diplomatic outcomes and solutions. They have developed strong cultural ties with the people of the mountain in Skoura, trading with them for ore and stone in exchange for military aid and sorcerous assistance.

Never particularly friendly to the Empire, they politely closed their borders against Imperial traders in 207YE. Prior to that there had been a few border skirmishes, but given their closest neighbours were the Urizen, these skirmishes rarely came to anything. In 330YE, diplomatic overtures from the Senator for [Spiral](../../in-character/nations/the-league/Spiral.md) were sent into Axos but rebuffed; it is believed that the Urizen were attempting to arrange a joint defence of that beleaguered territory but no records exist one way or another.

Category:Commission.title: Category:Commission
Category:Commission.body:
## Overview

The [Imperial Senate](../../mixed/government/senate/Senate.md) has the power to commission important projects or great works of construction that will benefit the Empire. Any Imperial citizen can make use of mithril, weirwood or white granite they have purchased to improve a resource they own. But regardless of how much wealth they possess, no citizen can recruit their own [army](../../out-of-character/rules/Army.md) or simply order the construction of a [great work](../../mixed/commissions/Great_work.md) unless they have been granted the authority to do so by a Senate motion.

Most commissions automatically result in the creation of a new [Imperial title](../../mixed/titles/Imperial_title.md), for example raising a new army causes the creation of a new Imperial [general](../../mixed/titles/General.md). Creating this title is an integral part of the commission and does not require a second motion to be considered by the Senate.

Category:Commonwealth.title: Category:Commonwealth
Category:Commonwealth.body:
*[Image: IconCommonwealth.jpg](https://www.profounddecisions.co.uk/empire-wiki/File:IconCommonwealth.jpg)*

## Overview

The Commonwealth is a young nation, taking its first major steps on the world stage. Guided by a philosophy of the greatest good for the greatest number of people, the nation is convinced that it can make the world a better place - a conviction that makes its neighbours very nervous. Three times in the last fifty years, the Commonwealth has been at war with nearby countries and in each case they have been victorious. Yet, rather than turning their conquered enemies into vassals, they have done everything possible to incorporate them into the greater Commonwealth. Membership brings a level of freedom and comfort seen in few other places - provided one is prepared to accept the philosophy of the greater good.

Like the Empire, the Commonwealth is dominated by humans (both [lineaged](../../mixed/magic/lore/Lineage.md) and unlineaged). Unlike the Empire, the Commonwealth population includes significant numbers of both [orcs](../../mixed/world/Orc.md) and [daeva](#look-and-feel) as well. Indeed, the Commonwealth recognises all sapient beings as having equal standing before their law, and equal opportunities within their society - a stance that contributes to their poor relations with the [Principalities of Jarm](../../in-character/foreign-nations/Principalities_of_Jarm.md).

Category:Curse.title: Category:Curse
Category:Curse.body:
*[Image: Many ritual curses are delivered with a damning indictment culminating in a terrible denunciation of their target.](https://www.profounddecisions.co.uk/empire-wiki/File:DOOOOM.jpg)*

## Overview

A curse is a persistent, harmful magical effect. Imperial lore contains many rituals that create curses. Most are not illegal although their use is overseen by the Imperial Conclave. Many eternals have been known to curse those who cross them, but curses can also be caused by malign magical creatures and sometimes just by exposure to magical forces that have run amok.

A target may be under any number of different curses at once.

Category:Egregore.title: Category:Egregore
Category:Egregore.body:
*[Image: Every nation has an egregore spirit, which bonds with one or more citizens of that nation and offers supporta nd guidance.](https://www.profounddecisions.co.uk/empire-wiki/File:Egregang.png)*

## Overview

Each nation has a single egregore spirit, created through ritual magic to represent the personification of the nation. The spirit may be present in more than one host body at any time. The ritual was created by the Brass Coast to ensure that the nations of the Empire retained their independent character and culture. In the game they act to encourage the players to maintain the visual and thematic identity of their nation. They are occasionally able to tell if a member of their nation is dead or alive.

Category:Eternals.title: Category:Eternals
Category:Eternals.body:
*[Image: Much of this information was collated by the Unfettered Mind in the Autumn and Winter of 386YE as part of their investigation into the influence of eternals on Imperial magic.](https://www.profounddecisions.co.uk/empire-wiki/File:OrderUnfetteredMind.jpg)*

## Overview

The eternals are the most powerful inhabitants of the six other [realms of existence](../../in-character/eternals/Realm.md). Some possess great temporal power commanding armies of soldiers, ruling great cities or claiming extensive lands in their realm. Others appear to be solitary individuals with only a few allies or servants. All of them have unique magical abilities that they can offer to those who deal with them, if the bargainer is prepared to pay the price.

Eternals, as the name implies, appear to be *mostly* immortal. They don't consistently age or change over time in any predictable way, and in some cases even the idea of death seems strange. While mortal magicians may argue the nature of [Phaleron](../../in-character/eternals/Phaleron.md), the being claims to be an actual library, and is completely unconcerned with life and death as a mortal might understand them. There are some eternals that seem to undergo significant changes, but their fundamental nature seems to remain the same. For example, [Basileia Brazen](../../in-character/eternals/Basileia.md) replaced Basileus Flint and seized control of the [City of Locks](../../in-character/eternals/Basileia.md), just as Flint replaced Basileus Kade years earlier. Through all these changes, though, the City of Locks endures and in each cycle it is ruled over by an eternal devoted to intrigue, power, and treachery.

> *In-character text:*
>
> > *In-character text:*
> >
> > Kill an eternal? How do you slay the wind? Swords may kill the peace, words may end the war, but conflict, like glory, is eternal.
> >
> > Morgause Erewash

There are exceptions: [Azoth](../../in-character/eternals/Azoth.md) apparently results from the union of two earlier eternals of the Night realm named [Murit](../../in-character/eternals/Murit.md) and [Soghter](../../in-character/eternals/Soghter.md), but in this case there is speculation that they are all the same creature undergoing a cyclic transformation as an expression of the fundamental nature of change. Likewise, the shifting prestige, power, and relationship of [Eleonaris](../../in-character/eternals/Eleonaris.md) and [Jaheris](../../in-character/eternals/Jaheris.md) seems to be an expression of the "duality" of nobility in the Summer realm.

What is clear is that eternals do not age, or change in a gradual way in the manner of mortal beings. When they change, the changes are fundamental and swift. An eternal that has presented the same face to the Empire for decades or centuries might suddenly change that face, but its new expression is tied inextricably to the underlying principles that form the core of its identity.

Not every eternal has the same level of interest in the Empire, but the [Conclave](../../mixed/government/conclave/Conclave.md) has the power to define the status of those that do via a [Declaration](../../mixed/government/conclave/Declaration.md) of [Alignment](../../in-character/eternals/Alignment.md). Doing so has a powerful but poorly understood [hearth magic](../../out-of-character/rules/Hearth_magic.md) effect that can make it more or less difficult for the eternal to use their powers to affect the Empire. A list of the current status of all eternals can be found [on that page](../../in-character/eternals/Alignment.md#status-of-eternals).

A list of eternals and their concerns can be found [here](Eternals.md#eternals-interested-in-the-empire). This list is not exhaustive. Rather it consists of those beings familiar to the Empire, usually because they have shown an interest in it at some point since its formation.

### Eternals Interested in the Empire

This list of eternals is not exhaustive; rather it lists some of those beings who have shown a special interest in the Empire since its formation.

The creature known as *Capradan, the Horned Hunter*, is a being of the Spring realm whose true nature is unclear. It is either a very potent herald or a lesser eternal concerned with primitive concepts of hunting and killing for sustenance. There is an eternal known in the [Sumaah Republic](../../in-character/foreign-nations/Sumaah_Republic.md) called *[Wind Panther](../../in-character/winds-of-fortune/Satraps_of_the_Abyss.md#of-spring)* that is not involved with the Empire.

The Sumaah Republic knows *[Span of the Sky](../../in-character/winds-of-fortune/Satraps_of_the_Abyss.md#of-day)* who may be the same eternal known in the [Sarcophan Delves](../../in-character/foreign-nations/Sarcophan_Delves.md) as *[Guadier, Lord of Winds](../../in-character/eternals/Eternals_of_the_sea.md#lord-of-the-winds)* associated with weather and currents.

The Sumaah Republic apparently associates with *[Deep Drummer](../../in-character/winds-of-fortune/Satraps_of_the_Abyss.md#of-night)*, who may be an aspect of [Janon](../../in-character/eternals/Janon.md) and deals with celebration and catharsis. In the Sarcophan Delves there are three Night eternals unknown in the Empire - *[Dathan](../../in-character/eternals/Eternals_of_the_sea.md#sailor-on-the-skerries), the Sailor on the Skerries (wonder, joy);* [Ungholt](../../in-character/eternals/Eternals_of_the_sea.md#hongerigespin-and-ungholt)*, the Delerium King (terror, nightmare, madness); and* Hongerigespin *(memory, forgetfulness, obfuscation). There is also reference to the* Lantern Shark *whose qualities are unknown.*

1. Prior to 384YE Ylenwe used the name Ylenrith and was strongly associated with purity.
2. In 382YE, two other eternals of the Night realm - [Murit](../../in-character/eternals/Murit.md) the Shaper and [Soghter](../../in-character/eternals/Soghter.md), Changer of the Ways - were unified into [Azoth](../../in-character/eternals/Azoth.md) with the assistance of Imperial magicians.

Category:Faraden.title: Category:Faraden
Category:Faraden.body:
## Overview

Faraden lies to the west of the Empire. It is a rocky, hilly nation on the far side of the Lasambrian hills. The Faraden are canny traders and fierce warriors. Up until very recently, the Faraden traded frequently with the [Freeborn](../../in-character/nations/the-brass-coast/The_Brass_Coast.md) at [Anduz](../../in-character/nations/the-brass-coast/Segura.md#anduz), but since the fall of [Segura](../../in-character/nations/the-brass-coast/Segura.md) in 363YE this has become a good deal more difficult. They are known to trade with their neighbours the [Iron Confederacy](../../in-character/foreign-nations/Iron_Confederacy.md), but also with lands to the south and west that are largely unvisited by Imperial traders - their nation serves as a “gateway” to the southwestern parts of the continent.

The people of Faraden have a lot in common with the Empire but are very independent. A major bone of contention is that their religion is closely related to the Imperial faith but includes elements that the [Synod](../../mixed/government/synod/Synod.md) believes is heretical, which helps make them extra touchy around Imperial citizens. They are often unprepared for what they see as the 'superior' attitude of their Imperial neighbours.

Category:Free Folk.title: Category:Free Folk
Category:Free Folk.body:
## Overview

The Free Folk is the name taken on by a group of refugees from the [Asavean Archipelago](../../in-character/foreign-nations/Asavean_Archipelago.md). They were evacuated at the tail end of the short-lived civil war from the satrapy of Marracossa. Early on, they were invited to live at [Caer Faucon](../../in-character/nations/dawn/Astolat.md#caer-faucon) by the [Lady of the Proffered Hand](../../mixed/titles/Lady_of_the_Proffered_Hand.md). They claim to be followers of the Way, but their particular take on the religion, and their peculiar [paragons and exemplars](../../mixed/government/synod/Paragons_and_exemplars.md) caused some tension in the Empire.

## Further Reading

A gonfalon is a [group magic item](../../out-of-character/rules/Magic_items.md#group-magic-items) that provides an advantage to a [banner](../../out-of-character/rules/Bands.md#banners). Category:Grand Inspiration.title: Category:Grand Inspiration
Category:Grand Inspiration.body:
## Overview

*[Image: Inspiration for the grand endeavour has been provided, the ground is being cleared, the first white granite towers begin to rise.](https://www.profounddecisions.co.uk/empire-wiki/File:Grand_Endeavours.png)*

Introduced in the [Blood will thicken](../../in-character/winds-of-fortune/Blood_will_thicken.md#a-question-of-scale) wind of fortune, the Grand Inspiration of the Way is an ambitious endeavour to transform the [White City of Bastion](../../in-character/nations/highguard/Bastion.md#bastion-the-white-city) into a grand sacred city dedicated to the Way. It would serve to cement the Empire as the foundation of the Way, and help to unify pilgrims under their version of the faith.

This category contains two broad classes of page:

A list of historical research projects commissioned since the start of the campaign can be found in the [recent historical research](../../mixed/government/senate/Historical_research.md#recent-historical-research) list.

## Overview

Each summit, The Throne can grant a single citizen the right to [address the Empire](../../mixed/titles/The_Throne.md#address-the-empire). The chosen citizen must provide the Imperial civil service with their words in writing over the following weeks. Their words will then be copied by scribes and spread throughout the land. The Throne may choose to address the Empire themselves or name any other Imperial citizen.

## Overview

An Imperial enchantment is an [enchantment](../../out-of-character/rules/Enchantment.md) created by [ritual](../../out-of-character/rules/Rituals.md) magic that targets the entire Empire. These enchantments are of particular interest to [Urizeni](../../in-character/nations/urizen/Urizen.md) [stargazers](../../in-character/nations/urizen/Stargazer.md) as they have special relevance to the theory of the [omnihedron](../../in-character/nations/urizen/Stargazer.md#resonance-and-the-omnihedron).

Category:Introduction.title: Category:Introduction
Category:Introduction.body:
## Overview

These pages try to provide a starting point for players new to live-roleplaying, or to the specific game of Empire. They cover some of our foundational concepts, and lay out some of the things that makes the Empire game - and the world it takes place in - unique.

Category:Iron Confederacy.title: Category:Iron Confederacy
Category:Iron Confederacy.body:
### Overview

The Iron Confederacy lies to the south-west of the Empire, beyond the [Brass Coast](../../in-character/nations/the-brass-coast/The_Brass_Coast.md). Their nation is made up of a number of large duchies allied in a loose confederacy. The northern duchies are heavily forested, while the western duchies are hilly and craggy rising to a low mountain range. The central duchies are warm, fertile plains that serve as a breadbasket for the rest of the nation.

The long coastline of the Iron Confederacy is particularly treacherous, and there are comparatively few areas within sight of land where large ships can travel safely. In many places sheer cliffs rise steeply, and in others there are great shoals of sharp rocks just below the surface.

The people of the Iron Confederacy call themselves the Suranni, the Children of Surann, and believe they are descendants of a divine forbear who ascended to heaven after founding their nation. Their noble families trace direct lines of descent to this deified ancestor. They are a highly warlike people, characterised by cruel and uncompromising nature, respect for martial might, suspicion of 'magic' and said to be envious of the Empire and indeed all other human nations.

Category:Jarm.title: Category:Jarm
Category:Jarm.body:
## Overview

The Principalities of Jarm are an old, confident nation that lies many weeks sailing to the east of the Empire. It is a little larger than the Empire, but regularly riven by internecine bickering between the various factions that rule there. It is often engaged in conflicts with the smaller nations that border it, occasionally engaging in wholesale wars of conquest against those neighbours for resources.

Category:Lineage.title: Category:Lineage
Category:Lineage.body:
## Overview

[Lineage](../../mixed/magic/lore/Lineage.md) is something that happens to humans - and only humans - who are "touched" in some fashion by the power of one of the six [realms](../../in-character/eternals/Realm.md) of magic. They are still human, but they possess physical trappings that differentiate them from their fellows. Lineaged people also experience urges toward certain behaviour as a consequence of the taint of magic in their blood. Within the Empire, lineaged people are treated the same as any other citizens, although people from specific nations may make assumptions about a person based on their lineage.

[orcs](../../mixed/world/Orc.md) never possess lineage.

## Magic Standards

A magic standard is a specific type of [talisman](../../out-of-character/rules/Magic_items.md#talisman). The phys-rep must be a banner or standard that is carried in the hand: it cannot be a back-banner or tabard. The banner pole must be at least 60" long, and the standard must be six square feet or more in area and at least one foot in any dimension (for example a 24" by 36" banner, or a 12" wide, 72" long pennant). You can include decorative additions to banners that are close to the minimum size to make them meet the requirements.

A standard must be wielded in at least one hand or it has no effect. You may not use a magic standard in the same hand as a shield or weapon. Regardless of construction, a standard cannot be used as a weapon nor may it be used to parry.

Category:Navarr Wayhouse.title: Category:Navarr Wayhouse
Category:Navarr Wayhouse.body:
## Overview

A [Navarr wayhouse](../../mixed/commissions/Navarr_wayhouse.md) is a large well-established [wayhouse](../../in-character/nations/navarr/Wayhouse.md) that has been built in a territory outside the Navarr nation. A wayhouse supports the stridings, serving as a place to rest and resupply. Its presence makes travel safer, boosting trade in the territory and allowing Navarr who live in that territory to benefit from communication, trade and support from the many stridings passing through.

As a result of the strengthened connections to the nation, Navarr resources in territories with a working wayhouse do not suffer the [usual penalty for being located in a foreign territory](../../out-of-character/rules/Resource.md#resources-in-other-nations). They benefit from any great works in the territory.

In addition, the Imperial civil service will formally identify the nearest Navarr territory to the wayhouse. Navarr citizens are eligible to [vote for a senator](../../in-character/nations/navarr/Navarr_leadership.md#leading-a-territory) as if their resources were in the linked territory.

| [Drawing the Penumbral Veil](../../mixed/magic/rituals/Drawing_the_Penumbral_Veil.md) | Shrouds a territory from scrying. | 8 |
| [Retrograde Wheel](../../out-of-character/game-design/Retrograde_Wheel.md) | Transforms three ingots or measures of materials the other way along an alchemical path. | 8 |
| [Ride the Noble Steed](../../mixed/magic/rituals/Ride_the_Noble_Steed.md) | Grants two people a vivid dream of riding a horse next time they sleep. | 8 |
| [Shadowed Glass of Sung](../../mixed/magic/rituals/Shadowed_Glass_of_Sung.md) | Divines mysterious, secretive, or enigmatic information about the immediate area. | 8 |

| [Twilight Masquerade](../../mixed/magic/rituals/The_Twilight_Masquerade.md) | Creates a magical disguise that changes lineage. | 8 |
| [Whispering Shadow Courtiers](../../mixed/magic/rituals/Whispering_Shadow_Courtiers.md) | Enables limited communication with the Whisper Gallery. | 8 |
| [Gardener's Wheel](../../mixed/magic/rituals/Gardener-s_Wheel.md) | Transforms up to five drams of the same herb along a specific path. | 10 |

| [Unfettered Anarchy](../../mixed/magic/rituals/Unfettered_Anarchy.md) | Curses a character with uncontrollable emotions. | 10 |

Category:Potions.title: Category:Potions
Category:Potions.body:
## Recipe List

There is a list of recipes known to Imperial apothecaries, which includes all of the following.

| Potion | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [Apothecary Potions](../../mixed/magic/potions/Apothecary_Potions.md) | Every apothecary knows how to mix these five preparations; they provide valuable medical aid. |
| [Balms of the Fountainhead](../../mixed/magic/potions/Balms_of_the_Fountainhead.md) | Ointments that increase the power of ritualists to wield Spring lore. |
| [Decoctions of Hoarfrost](../../mixed/magic/potions/Decoctions_of_Hoarfrost.md) | Preparations that increase the power of Winter ritualists. |
| [Double-sided Blade](../../mixed/magic/potions/Double-sided_Blade.md) | Preparations that allow a character to survive lethal blows but with a significant cost. |
| [Infusions of Feathers](../../mixed/magic/potions/Infusions_of_Feathers.md) | Mysterious infusions that grant supernatural insight to those who breath their mystic fumes. |
| [Lambent Essences](../../mixed/magic/potions/Lambent_Essences.md) | Methodical elixirs that increase the power of ritualists to wield Day magic. |
| [Legacy of Thorns](../../mixed/magic/potions/Legacy_of_Thorns.md) | Toxic preparations that weaken and envenom, used on weapons or to poison the unwary. |
| [Magnum Opus](../../mixed/magic/potions/Magnum_Opus.md) | Mysterious preparations that increase the power of ritualists to wield Night magic. |
| [Master Medicinal](../../mixed/magic/potions/Master_Medicinal.md) | Specialist medicinal potions that restore groups of people or provide multiple healing benefits in one swallow. |
| [Philtres of the High Peaks](../../mixed/magic/potions/Philtres_of_the_High_Peaks.md) | Potions that restore the personal mana of magicians, or drain it completely. |
| [Philtres of War](../../mixed/magic/potions/Philtres_of_War.md) | Potions that restore hero points and bolster a character's fighting spirit - or remove it. |
| [Runa's Gift](../../mixed/magic/potions/Runa-s_Gift.md) | Potions that allow [orcs](../../mixed/world/Orc.md) to perform magical acts. |
| [The Assassin's Gate](../../mixed/magic/potions/The_Assassin-s_Gate.md) | Lethal ingested poisons that cause swift, painful death - and their antidotes. |
| [The Last Resort](../../mixed/magic/potions/The_Last_Resort.md) | Lethal ingested poisons captured from the Druj that cause sickness and agonising death - and their antidotes. |
| [The Winter Moon](../../mixed/magic/potions/The_Winter_Moon.md) | Lethal ingested poisons that cause madness and lingering death - and their antidotes. |
| [Tisanes of the Labyrinth](../../mixed/magic/potions/Tisanes_of_the_Labyrinth.md) | Liao-based preparations that empower religious ceremonies with extra strength. |
| [Tonics of the Deep Forest](../../mixed/magic/potions/Tonics_of_the_Deep_Forest.md) | Potions that enhance a character's ability to take damage, allowing them to shrug off wounds that might otherwise incapacitate them. |
| [Tonics of the Open Sky](../../mixed/magic/potions/Tonics_of_the_Open_Sky.md) | Potions that give enhanced fortitude; the extra time they grant mortally wounded characters has saved many lives. |
| [Tinctures of True Eminence](../../mixed/magic/potions/Tinctures_of_True_Eminence.md) | Heady elixirs that increase the power of ritualists to wield Summer magic. |
| [Unguents of Falling Leaves](../../mixed/magic/potions/Unguents_of_Falling_Leaves.md) | Exotic preparations that increase the power of ritualists to wield Autumn magic. |
| [Unshackled Gift](../../mixed/magic/potions/Unshackled_Gift.md) | Potent preparations that allow [orcs](../../mixed/world/Orc.md) to perform heroic acts. |

## Overview

This category collects [rituals](../../out-of-character/rules/Rituals.md) that target various [personal resources](../../out-of-character/rules/Resource.md#personal-resource). Most are [enchantments](../../out-of-character/rules/Enchantment.md) that are performed on the character who owns the personal resource, using the [Law of Dominion](../../out-of-character/rules/Laws_of_magic.md#the-law-of-dominion) to transfer the magic to the resource without actually enchanting the character themselves. The actual effects vary; some make the resource more productive or change their production while others have more esoteric powers such as hiding a resource from enemies or allowing one resource to act as if it were another.

All these rituals are part of either [Imperial lore](../../out-of-character/rules/Formulaic_ritual.md#imperial-lore-and-the-ritual-list) or [Urizen lore](../../in-character/nations/urizen/Urizen_magical_traditions.md#urizen-lore).

Category:Sarcophan.title: Category:Sarcophan
Category:Sarcophan.body:
*[Image: Bladeroot.jpg](https://www.profounddecisions.co.uk/empire-wiki/File:Bladeroot.jpg)*

## Overview

Far to the south of the Bay of Catazar, on the wide, winding delta of the Umshalla River lies the tottering ramshackle city of Sarcophan. More commonly referred to as the Delves, this great metropolis is said to be home to both the wealthiest, and the poorest, people in the world. The Bedelaar Huisbaas (usually rendered as 'beggar kings' in Imperial, or abbreviated to Bedelaar) of Sarcophan head great merchant families whose wealth is founded on the bounty they harvested from the tombs of their predecessors centuries ago. A relatively young nation, whose people see wealth as the highest aspirations, the Sarcophan have a not-entirely-undeserved reputation for ruthless pursuit of profit regardless of the cost.

The Sarcophan Delves occupy the mouth of a great river, on the northern shores of a continent that is largely unknown to Imperial explorers. The nations near Sarcophan seem to view the city, and the people who live there, as accursed. There have been several wars and skirmishes between the Sarcophan and their neighbours, often using mercenary troops. For the most part, the Sarcophan people are markedly outward-looking, seeking beyond their borders for any opportunity to turn a profit and increase their own fortunes, and the fortunes of their houses. Sarcophan explorers and merchants might be encountered in almost any part of the known world.

Of particular interest to Imperial citizens is the role Sarcophan plays as a [port](../../mixed/economy/Foreign_ports.md#sarcophan-delves), open to trade with the Empire. The Sarcophan Delves are also the source of the [ilium](../../out-of-character/rules/Ilium.md) provided by the [Steel Fist](../../mixed/titles/Steel_Fist.md) Seat on the [Bourse](../../mixed/economy/Bourse.md). The swamps and marshes are said to have a number of very rich deposits of this rare material.

In Summer 383YE a joint historical research project with some Sarcophan scholars confirmed that the [origins of the Highborn](../../in-character/nations/highguard/Origins_of_the_Highborn.md) lay in the city of Sarcophan.

Category:Senate.title: Category:Senate
Category:Senate.body:
*[Image: With the assistance of the civil service, the Senate make significant choices about the future of the Empire.](https://www.profounddecisions.co.uk/empire-wiki/File:Genial_Conversation.jpg)*

## Overview

The [Imperial Senate](../../mixed/government/senate/Senate.md) is the primary legislative body for the Empire. It is an elective chamber; with one [senator](../../mixed/titles/Senator.md) appointed by each territory of the Empire to represent their interests. The chamber has access to a wide range of political powers which makes senators some of the most powerful political individuals in the Empire. They alone have the ability to change Imperial law, as well as enjoying access to the Imperial treasury. They are also responsible for appointing [The Throne](../../mixed/titles/The_Throne.md), along with a number of other [titles](../../mixed/titles/Imperial_title.md); they [commission](../../mixed/commissions/Commission.md) structures such as [sinecures](../../mixed/commissions/Sinecure.md) and [great works](../../mixed/commissions/Great_work.md); raise [armies](../../out-of-character/rules/Army.md); ratify treaties; and otherwise make significant choices about the future of the Empire.

This selection of articles can be **[downloaded as a PDF book](https://www.profounddecisions.co.uk/mediawiki-public/index.php?title=Category:Senate&action=pdfbook)** (or as [html only](https://www.profounddecisions.co.uk/mediawiki-public/index.php?title=Category:Senate&action=pdfbook&format=html))

Category:Senate Sessions.title: Category:Senate Sessions
Category:Senate Sessions.body:
*[Image: The civil service record and publish the details of each Senate session.](https://www.profounddecisions.co.uk/empire-wiki/File:Speaker_Elodie.jpg)*

## Overview

Like the [Conclave](../../mixed/government/conclave/Conclave.md) and the [Military Council](../../mixed/government/military/Military_Council.md), the [Senate](../../mixed/government/senate/Senate.md) conducts its official business at formal sessions, where matters are discussed and votes are cast. Although members of the Senate meet to discuss business throughout the day (the [Speaker for the Senate](../../mixed/titles/Speaker_for_the_Senate.md) encourages all members to discuss Senate in advance of the session), the sessions are the best chance to address the entire Senate and the only time that motions can be raised and voted upon. Traditionally, the Senate aims to have have two sessions each full day of an Imperial summit and one session each half-day.

Following each summit, the [motions](../../in-character/senate-motions/Senate_motion.md) raised and voted on during the Solstice or Equinox are collected together and made public knowledge by the civil service.

Category:Sentinel Gate.title: Category:Sentinel Gate
Category:Sentinel Gate.body:
*[Image: The Sentinel Gate is an ancient magical device that allows Imperial heroes to travel to specific locations around the Empire to intervene in events at propitious moments.](https://www.profounddecisions.co.uk/empire-wiki/File:Sentinel_at_the_Gate.jpg)*

## Overview

The Sentinel Gate is the massive archway that stands at one side of Anvil. It is used by Imperial citizens to teleport to battle-grounds to fight the barbarians - as well as to go on quests throughout the Empire.

## Conjunctions

The power of the stars creates connections between times and places - referred to by Imperial magicians as *conjunctions*. By using the Gate to access a conjunction a character can travel from Anvil to the site linked through the conjunction. The device is powerful and expensive, but not so powerful that it could not be replicated. However the Gate does not *create* conjunctions - it only provides the means to access them, so creating an additional Gate would not generate any additional conjunctions.

The Sentinel Gate at Anvil was bonded to the Empire centuries ago by Urizen magicians using a powerful Autumn ritual. Because of this, only Imperial citizens can use the Gate. Autumn magic can be used to create a link between the Empire and a barbarian or a foreigner to allow them to use the Gate - and Night magic can transform or disguise a target in such a way that they can pass through. In both cases, it requires that those using the Gate are accompanied by a greater number of Imperial citizens. In the opinion of Imperial magicians, the Gate is secure from intrusion - a belief supported by the last four centuries of use.

Partly as a result of this bond, the Gate can only be used to travel to places the Empire is connected to - either inside the Empire, on the borders or to locations where significant numbers of Imperial troops are present. In theory, the bond could be broken but it would then need bonding to a new nation or power to be usable at all.

Category:Sumaah.title: Category:Sumaah
Category:Sumaah.body:
*[Image: IconSumaah.jpg](https://www.profounddecisions.co.uk/empire-wiki/File:IconSumaah.jpg)*

## Overview

Before the Empire, missionaries of the nascent Way came to the jungles of Sumaah and called it 'the ends of the earth.' They found a corrupt, diseased kingdom ruled by despotic kings supported by a selfish and idolatrous religion, propped up by the satraps of the [Asavean Archipelago](../../in-character/foreign-nations/Asavean_Archipelago.md). Yet they also found embers of their own faith, hidden in old stories and legends. They fanned those embers, and without warning ignited a revolution. A people sickened by the excesses of their leaders, hungry for a philosophy of truth, took the teachings of [the Way](../../in-character/world/The_Way.md) and forged a sword with which they swept away the corrupt and the greedy and built something new, and better.

For nearly a century, emissaries and diplomats travelled the vast distances between Sumaah and the Empire. Few pilgrims managed to make the arduous journey to [Highguard](../../in-character/nations/highguard/Highguard.md), but those who did were increasingly dissatisfied with what they found - compromise, expediency, and tolerance were poisoning the roots of the shared faith. The Sumaash had no interest in joining the Empire, and so were denied a place in the [Synod](../../mixed/government/synod/Synod.md); indeed, they saw little in the Imperial Synod that was relevant to them - the virtues of [Ambition](../../in-character/religion/Ambition.md) and [Pride](../../in-character/religion/Pride.md) made it clear to these fervent converts that to look to an outside source for guidance would be wicked.

Eventually the Sumaash had had enough. In 118YE, during the reign of [Empress Aenea](../../in-character/history/Empress_Aenea.md), the Republic broke with the [Synod](../../mixed/government/synod/Synod.md) and technically excommunicated not only the Empress but all the priests of the Empire. The Empire was technically at war with the Sumaah Republic for the next two hundred years, but the vast distances involved meant that military conflict was all but impossible. All trade between the Republic and the Empire ceased, however, and it was not until 326YE that the trade routes were re-opened.

Today, the Sumaash are a great power. Their ambition is limitless; they regularly engage in wars of conquest with their neighbours. converting them to the faith by sword and spear. Those who will not convert are given a simple choice to leave, or die. They burn with the fire of the zealot, and those who live near them look with some concern towards their borders. Still, they are far away, and while some priests of the Synod insist on debating what they call the Sumaah problem, for most of the Empire they are little more than another exotic foreign nation, far away, that just happens to have a faith in common with the Empire.

Of particular interest to Imperial citizens outside of the Synod are the [Sumaash ports](../../mixed/economy/Foreign_ports.md#sumaah-republic) which are open to trade with the Empire.

*[Image: This picture appears on the page for any ritual that is part of Urizen lore rather than Imperial lore .](https://www.profounddecisions.co.uk/empire-wiki/File:NBUrizen.jpg)*

## Urizen Lore

Urizen lore (named in the same manner as [Imperial lore](../../out-of-character/rules/Formulaic_ritual.md#imperial-lore-and-the-ritual-list)) is a special body of magical knowledge supported with the assistance of the [eternal](../../in-character/eternals/Eternal.md) [Phaleron](../../in-character/eternals/Phaleron.md). It functions in a very similar manner to Imperial lore, but only citizens of Urizen can master the rituals contained within it. Even if an individual Urizen magician has not mastered one of these rituals, they may still perform it, just as any other Imperial citizen can perform a ritual that is part of [Imperial lore](../../out-of-character/rules/Rituals.md#imperial-lore).

The lynchpin of Urizen lore is the [Grand Library of Canterspire](../../in-character/nations/urizen/Morrow.md#canterspire), a magical library in [Morrow](../../in-character/nations/urizen/Morrow.md) that is operated by the [eternals](../../in-character/eternals/Eternal.md) of the Celestial Library in conjunction with the people of Urizen.

Adding a ritual to Urizen lore requires the [ritual text](../../out-of-character/rules/Formulaic_ritual.md#ritual-texts) to be the target of the [Gift of Knowledge](../../in-character/winds-of-fortune/The_way_that_the_sunshine_gleams.md#a-new-archives) ritual. Rather than being returned to the caster, the ritual is added to the body of Urizen lore and becomes available to every Urizen magician following the summit where the ritual is added to lore.

It is not possible for the [Conclave](../../mixed/government/conclave/Conclave.md) to use a [declaration](../../mixed/government/conclave/Declaration.md) of [dissemination](../../mixed/government/conclave/Dissemination.md) or [Imperial lore](../../mixed/government/conclave/Imperial_lore.md) to affect a ritual that is part of Urizen lore, nor is it possible to either remove a ritual from Urizen lore, nor to recover the ritual text once it has been added to the body of knowledge.

A former Urizen citizen who leaves the nation loses access to rituals that are part of Urizen lore; they can be replaced using the normal process of changing mastery.

Category:Vallorn.title: Category:Vallorn
Category:Vallorn.body:
*[Image: A vallorn seems to be a malignant hostile magical ecosystem.](https://www.profounddecisions.co.uk/empire-wiki/File:Blood_for_Poppies.jpg)*

## Overview

The vallorn appeared as part of the disaster that overthrew the cities of a nation named as 'Terunael' in Navarr legends, which may have covered much of the land which is now Empire. From the hearts of those cities, abundant greenery spread, a sick, infectious wave of life that cracked and crumbled stone, shot great trees up through streets and buildings, and warped, twisted and destroyed most of the inhabitants of those cities, scattering the others to the wind.

> *In-character text:*
>
> > *In-character text:*
> >
> > The Vallorn... nothing less than the vile offspring spewed out from the mating of a Great White Shark and a rampant fungal infection.
> >
> > Zietel van Temeschwar, Mountebank

As the refugees attempted to claim back their lands, they discovered that around the core of each city, areas of superabundant, warped life had appeared, resistant to all efforts to destroy them. These were named vallorn.

A vallorn seems to be a malignant hostile magical ecosystem -- an area deep in the heart of a forest where even the Navarr fear to tread. Inside them are monstrous plants, the spores of which mutate living creatures that are exposed over many months. Even the air is different within the vallorn, weakening those who enter as if they were breathing mild poison. The plants that grow there often have supernatural capabilities; [chaos fruit](../../out-of-character/rules/Chaos_fruit.md) are an example of vegetation that has been infused both with vallorn essence and powerful [Spring magic](../../out-of-character/rules/Spring_magic.md) but there are many others. Some of the plants are even predators in their own right.

Category:Warfare.title: Category:Warfare
Category:Warfare.body:
## Overview

This category collects [rituals](../../out-of-character/rules/Rituals.md) that are relevant to [war](../../out-of-character/rules/War.md), and the military campaign. Most are [enchantments](../../out-of-character/rules/Enchantment.md) that target either an [Imperial army](../../out-of-character/rules/Army.md) or a [military unit](../../out-of-character/rules/Military_unit.md) [personal resource](../../out-of-character/rules/Resource.md#personal-resource). although there are also several [curses](../../out-of-character/rules/Curse.md) that have implications for armies and [navies](../../out-of-character/rules/Navy.md).

All these rituals are part of either [Imperial lore](../../out-of-character/rules/Formulaic_ritual.md#imperial-lore-and-the-ritual-list) or [Urizen lore](../../in-character/nations/urizen/Urizen_magical_traditions.md#urizen-lore).

Category:Winds of Magic.title: Category:Winds of Magic
Category:Winds of Magic.body:
## Overview

Winds of Magic is a classification of Wind of Fortune that primarily deals with magical matters - generally [eternals](../../in-character/eternals/Eternal.md), events significant to Imperial magicians, or the business of the [Conclave](../../mixed/government/conclave/Conclave.md). At any given event there may be any number of winds of fortune dealing with magical events or beings, but the Winds of Magic serve as a "roundup" of shorter pieces of information themed around magical effects or eternals.
